default.statement: Every rule that can stop a flow (refuse, fail a gate, block a merge) has an active record in rules.catalog with every field, and scripts/rule check counts as numbers the records with gaps, past their review date or end condition, with an unanswered question, never measured or without a root cause, or resting on an unsettled or missing premise, and the stopping functions rules.stop_patterns finds that no record lists; while rules.check_mode is report it refuses nothing.

created.by: A Torre, RULE-AUDIT rule system (Daniel's order of 16:52 and 16:55 BRT; D-069 item 9, D-072)

ends_when.text: Report mode ends when an approved decision flips rules.check_mode to refuse: this non-stopping record is then retired (retired.by names that decision) and replaced by a stopping record (stops true) that carries damage_if_passed and impact_of_removal.

default.damage_if_passed: A rule that can stop a flow runs with no justification, owner, review date or end condition, or outlives its reason or its premise, and nothing counts it.

impact_of_removal.positive: Whoever writes a stopping rule writes no record and keeps no review date; the registry carries one file fewer.
impact_of_removal.negative: Rules exist again without a justification, owner, review date, end condition or premise; a rule past its review date, past its end condition or resting on a refuted premise stops being a number anyone sees.
impact_of_removal.measured: Not measured: the system starts in report mode on 2026-10-28 with no history. What would measure it: the counts of scripts/rule check --json over successive runs (unregistered stops, records with gaps, due, ending, rules on stale premises) and the time the check adds to a gate run.

question.text: Why does the rule register exist, who asked for it, what breaks without it, and when does its report mode end?

answers.text: Daniel ordered it on 2026-10-28 (16:52 and 16:55 BRT, with 17:08 and 17:09): every rule that can stop a flow needs a justification, an owner, a review date, an end condition, its premises, a standing question and, when it stops, a root cause. Without it a stopping rule runs unexamined and outlives its reason with nothing counting it. Report mode ends when an approved decision flips rules.check_mode to refuse (ends_when).

description: One record per rule that can stop a flow (RULE-AUDIT rule system, Daniel 2026-10-28 16:52, 16:55, 17:08 and 17:09 BRT): id R-<kebab>; statement (one sentence); where (path:function or path#key refs to the code or config that implements it); owner (D-NNN, or a named person and a date); created {on, by}; review_by and the optional last_reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD); ends_when {kind manual|date|path_exists|path_absent|registry_equals, text, plus on, path, or key and equals}; stops; damage_if_passed; impact_of_removal {positive, negative, measured}; premises (P-NN of docs/process/premises); question {text, answers [{on, by, text}]}, the standing question every rule answers at any time; stop_record {count (null: never measured), source, measured_on, root_cause, cheapest_fix} for a rule that stops; status active|retired, and a retired record keeps retired {on, by D-NNN, reason}. This schema checks the shape; scripts/rule check counts the missing fields, dates, end conditions, answers, stop records and premises and refuses nothing while rules.check_mode is report.
